{"consolidated_memory":"## Duplicate Charge in Webhook Consumer: 8 Incidents in billing/webhooks/stripe.py

Recurring problem across 8 separate occasions (2026-04-10 through 2026-08-15) of duplicate rows appearing in the ledger when the same webhook ID is redelivered. Each incident manifested in a different subset of traffic and had a distinct root cause. All covered by tests/billing/test_stripe_webhook.py.

**Incident 1: [2026-04-10]**
- Manifestation: OAuth provider sessions only
- Signal: Two ledger rows sharing one event ID
- Root cause: Naive datetime compared against aware datetime
- Fix: Made every boundary timezone aware at edge (PR #1801, branch fix/duplicate-charge-1)
- Result: 88 duplicate rows per day stopped being written

**Incident 2: [2026-04-11]**
- Manifestation: Clients pinned to v1 SDK only
- Signal: Two ledger rows sharing one event ID
- Root cause: Race condition in lazy initialisation
- Fix: Guarded initialisation with double-checked lock (PR #1983, branch fix/duplicate-charge-2)
- Result: Nightly rollup matched source counts for 72 consecutive days

**Incident 3: [2026-05-05]**
- Manifestation: Traffic arriving through corporate proxy only
- Signal: Two ledger rows sharing one event ID
- Root cause: Mutable default argument shared across calls
- Fix: Made default empty and built value per call (PR #4463, branch fix/duplicate-charge-3)
- Result: p99 latency fell from 6.6 seconds to 121 ms

**Incident 4: [2026-05-09]**
- Manifestation: Accounts in the five percent rollout bucket only
- Signal: Two ledger rows sharing one event ID
- Root cause: Connection pool exhaustion under burst load
- Fix: Raised pool ceiling and put bounded wait queue in front of it (PR #5456, branch fix/duplicate-charge-4)
- Result: Error rate dropped from 1.1 percent to under 6 per ten thousand

**Incident 5: [2026-06-12]**
- Manifestation: First request after cold start only
- Signal: Two ledger rows sharing one event ID
- Root cause: Schema drift between database migration and model
- Fix: Regenerated model from migration and pinned checksum (PR #6307, branch fix/duplicate-charge-5)
- Result: Memory settled at 363 MB instead of climbing past 7 GB

**Incident 6: [2026-06-29]**
- Manifestation: Tenants with more than ten thousand distinct keys only
- Signal: Two ledger rows sharing one event ID
- Root cause: Listener registered but never removed on teardown
- Fix: Removed listener on teardown and added assertion in test (PR #7391, branch fix/duplicate-charge-6)
- Result: Job finished in 77 minutes instead of 8 hours

**Incident 7: [2026-08-01]**
- Manifestation: Traffic after rolling restart of fleet only
- Signal: Two ledger rows sharing one event ID
- Root cause: Missing Unicode normalisation before hashing
- Fix: Normalised to NFC ahead of digest (PR #8678, branch fix/duplicate-charge-7)
- Result: Throughput rose 66 percent to 277 requests per second

**Incident 8: [2026-08-15]**
- Manifestation: Jobs scheduled across the midnight boundary only
- Signal: Two ledger rows sharing one event ID
- Root cause: Missing composite index on (tenant_id, created_at)
- Fix: Added composite index and backfilled in batches (PR #9245, branch fix/duplicate-charge-8)
- Result: Reclaimed 99 GB of blob storage

**Common attributes across all incidents:**
- File: billing/webhooks/stripe.py (billing side)
- Reproducibility: Redeliver the same webhook ID twice
- Problem signature: Two ledger rows sharing one event ID
- Stack: Python
- Test coverage: tests/billing/test_stripe_webhook.py"}
